title: Entitlement Archival and Revocation Workflow
author: Avery Chen
content:
Purpose
This document defines a cross-functional workflow for entitlement archival and revocation across Redwood Inference: how access is revoked, how artifacts are archived for compliance, how audit logs are correlated, and how the SDLC and incident response processes are triggered. The playbook balances forensic readiness, data-residency constraints, and the need to rapidly remediate risk.

Scope
- Applies to user and service entitlements for all production systems (hosted API, Dedicated, Private)
- Covers automatic revocation, manual emergency revocation, evidence packaging, and archival retention for audits
- Excludes non-production sandbox accounts unless explicitly flagged as production-mirroring

Definitions
- Entitlement: any RBAC grant (role assignment, policy binding, OAuth scope, service token) allowing access to production resources
- Revocation Event: a trigger that initiates entitlement removal (deprovision, role change, incident containment)
- Evidence Bundle: packaged artifacts (audit logs, approval records, snapshots) required for regulatory or legal review

Owners & Roles
- Security Response (owner): validates revocation, classifies event severity, coordinates evidence packaging
- Identity & Access (I&A): performs entitlement removal, issues attestation, updates entitlement ledger
- SRE / Platform: ensures audit log retention and snapshotting; provides system-level snapshots on request
- Legal & Compliance: approves long-term archival beyond standard retention windows
- Service Owners: confirm business impact and accept rollback requests

High-level Workflow (summary)
1. Detect: Revocation Event occurs (automation rule, attestation expiry, manual request, incident).
2. Assess: Security Response classifies scope and required containment level.
3. Revoke: I&A removes entitlement; system tokens rotated; access gates applied.
4. Collect: SRE collects audit logs, configuration snapshots, approval records.
5. Package: Security assembles Evidence Bundle according to residency rules.
6. Archive: Evidence moved to retention store; retention metadata recorded in evidence index.
7. Follow-up: Post-revocation validation, SLA closure, optional legal hold.

Detailed Procedures
A. Detection and Triage
- Automated triggers (examples):
  - Entitlement age > 90 days without recent use AND role flagged as high-privilege
  - JIT token request denied rate > 2x baseline
  - Incident playbook marker: suspected privilege escalation
- Manual requests: Service owners or auditors file a Revocation Request in the access portal (step ID generated)
- Triage checklist (security):
  1) Confirm the identity and scope of the entitlement
  2) Identify systems affected and data residency implications
  3) Assign event severity (Low / Medium / High / Critical)

B. Revocation Mechanics
- For user accounts: disable primary login, remove role bindings, rotate personal access tokens and API keys
- For service accounts: rotate service credentials, revoke OAuth client secrets, and update service-to-service allow lists
- For ephemeral JIT grants: revoke active sessions and purge KV caches where session tokens are persisted
- Timing: High / Critical events perform immediate revocation (0–5 min). Medium/Low: scheduled revocation during maintenance window if required.

C. Evidence Collection & Packaging
- Evidence Bundle must contain (minimum):
  - Authorization decision logs (policy evaluation events) covering 48 hours prior to revocation
  - Audit entries for entitlement creation, modification, and attestation history
  - CI/CD release references if entitlements were modified by automation (pipeline run IDs)
  - Configuration snapshot (role definitions, group memberships, policy JSON) at time-of-revocation
  - Screenshots or exports of approval records where available
  - Chain-of-approval metadata (who approved, when, justification)
- Packaging format: compressed tar.gz containing a manifest.json (see example below)

Sample manifest.json (stringified for reference):
{
  "revocation_id": "REV-2026-00123",
  "initiator": "i.a.kumar@redwood.example",
  "service": "inference-gateway",
  "affected_entitlements": ["role:artifact-uploader"],
  "evidence_files": ["authz-decisions.log", "role-defs-2026-06-02.json"],
  "retention_policy": "standard-7y"
}

D. Data Residency & Retention Mapping
- Determine residency by mapping the affected system to the customer and deployment region. If evidence contains customer PII or model inputs that are in-scope for residency controls, apply geo-fenced archival.
- Retention tier table:
| Retention Tier | Duration | Evidence Types | Approval Required |
| standard-3y | 3 years | entitlement logs, role defs | Security Lead |
| standard-7y | 7 years | legal hold, cross-border incidents | Legal + CISO |
| ephemeral-90d | 90 days | routine revocations with no data exposure | I&A Owner |

E. Audit Logging Requirements
- Required fields for every authorization event: timestamp (ISO8601), request_id, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource, decision (allow/deny), policy_id, evaluation_context_hash
- TTL and storage: primary hot store (30 days), cold store (3 years), deep-archive (7 years+) when legal hold applies
- Audit index labels: revocation_id, related_incident, customer_tenant_id, residency_region

F. SDLC Gates & Secure Release Integration
- Any automated entitlement change triggered by CI/CD must pass the following gates before deployment to prod:
  1) Approval step recorded in pipeline (non-skipable)
  2) Automated policy-simulator (no regressions)
  3) Smoke test that validates minimal privilege post-change
- If an entitlement revocation originates from an emergency incident and requires a rollback of a release, reference the release_id in the Evidence Bundle and follow the emergency release rollback runbook.

G. Incident Response Hooks
- If revocation is part of a Critical incident:
  - Security Response opens an Incident Evidence ticket and signals Legal for immediate hold
  - SRE snapshots ephemeral storage, datastore indexes, and KV caches and exports them into the Evidence Bundle
  - I&A freezes cross-system syncs to avoid auto-provisioning re-enabling access

H. Compliance Evidence Handoff (packaging & delivery)
- Steps to deliver an Evidence Bundle to auditors/regulators:
  1) Validate manifest and checksums (SHA256)
  2) Redact customer-identifiable fields if regulator permits; document redactions in manifest
  3) Store bundle in restricted archival bucket with MFA-delete enabled
  4) Record delivery in the Evidence Index (revocation_id, owner, retention_tier, delivered_to)
  5) Notify stakeholders with secure link and timebound access window

I. Exception & Risk Handling
- Short-term exception: allow extension of access for 72 hours with explicit justification captured, second-level approval, and compensating controls (session monitoring, tag audit logs)
- Long-term exception: requires risk review board approval, documented mitigation plan, and quarterly attestation until exception sunset

J. Post-Action Validation & Metrics
- Post-revocation checklist (I&A + SRE):
  - Confirm no active sessions remain for the revoked principal
  - Verify policy simulator shows no unexpected allow paths
  - Confirm audit logs show expected deny decisions for subsequent access attempts
- KPIs tracked monthly: mean time-to-revoke (target < 10 minutes for Critical), evidence package completeness rate (> 99%), number of exception re-approvals

Automation Examples
- Revoke user role via CLI (example):
  redwood-iam revoke --principal user:alice --role artifact-uploader --reason "compromised-key" --revocation-id REV-2026-00123

- Collect audit slice (example):
  redwood-logs query --service inference-gateway --from "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z" --to "2026-06-02T00:00:00Z" --filter revocation_id=REV-2026-00123 --output ./evidence/authz-decisions.log

- Pack bundle (example):
  tar -czf REV-2026-00123.tgz manifest.json authz-decisions.log role-defs-2026-06-02.json && sha256sum REV-2026-00123.tgz > REV-2026-00123.sha256

Audit & Review Cadence
- Monthly internal spot-checks of random revocation events to verify evidence completeness and retention tagging
- Quarterly tabletop exercises with SRE, I&A, Legal to simulate revocation + evidence delivery under cross-border constraints

Appendices
- Appendix A: Evidence manifest field descriptions
  - revocation_id: unique event ID
  - initiator: authenticated principal that initiated revocation
  - retention_policy: canonical tier
